title: The Future of Agency: AI SEO with Will Scott
subtitle: Navigating the AI-Powered Search Landscape
speaker_notes: Welcome everyone. I'm Will Scott, founder of Search Influence. For the next 45 minutes, we're going to talk about the biggest shift in search since Google's founding - and what it means for agencies like yours. This isn't theoretical - this is happening right now, and the agencies that adapt first will have a massive competitive advantage.

title: From Search to Synthesis
subtitle: How AI Is Rewriting Visibility
bullets: The paradigm shift every agency must understand
speaker_notes: We're moving from a world where search engines ranked pages to a world where AI synthesizes answers. That changes everything - how we optimize, what we measure, and how we prove value to clients. By the end of this presentation, you'll have a clear framework for navigating this transition.

title: About Will Scott & Search Influence
subtitle: 20 years in digital marketing
bullets: Founder & CEO, Search Influence • 9× Inc 5000 honoree • SMX Master Class instructor • Tagline: "We optimize potential"
speaker_notes: Quick context on who I am: I've been in digital marketing for 20 years, built Search Influence into a 9-time Inc 5000 company, and I teach the SMX Master Class on AI search optimization. Our mission at Search Influence is simple: "We optimize potential" - and that's never been more important than right now.

title: The Only Constant Is Change
subtitle: Opening Story & Conflict
bullets: The only constant is change. — Heraclitus
speaker_notes: Let's start with an ancient truth. Heraclitus said this 2,500 years ago, and it's never been more relevant to SEO. Every decade brings a major shift - and every shift creates new winners and new losers. We're in one of those shifts right now.

title: AI "Wow" Moment
subtitle: My AI Wake-Up Call
bullets: Testing ChatGPT for the first time • Asked: "Who are the leaders in local SEO?" • Realized: Traffic metrics suddenly incomplete • The moment everything changed
speaker_notes: STORY TIME: I'll never forget the first time I asked ChatGPT "Who are the leaders in local SEO?" It gave me a comprehensive answer, synthesized from dozens of sources, with no links to click. And I thought: "Wait - if this is how people search now, then traffic, CTR, bounce rate... all the metrics we've been optimizing for... they're becoming less relevant." That was my "oh no" moment. But then I realized - there's a new metric that matters: citation. Being referenced, being the source, being the authority AI quotes.

title: The Goal Shift: Traffic → Citation
subtitle: The Old Goal vs The New Goal
bullets: OLD GOAL: Rank #1, Get the click, Drive traffic, Measure pageviews • NEW GOAL: Be the source, Earn the citation, Build authority, Measure mentions
speaker_notes: PAUSE HERE. This is the mental shift that changes everything. For 25 years, we optimized for clicks. Now we optimize for citations. Traffic is still important - but visibility is more important. Being mentioned in an AI-generated answer reaches users we'll never see in our analytics. This is the new game.

title: Before vs After SERP
subtitle: The SERP You Know vs The SERP That's Coming
bullets: Left: Traditional 10 blue links • Right: AI Overview dominating, organic pushed down
speaker_notes: Look at the difference. On the left - the SERP we've optimized for since the '90s. On the right - what users actually see in 2025. That AI Overview at the top? It's not just one result - it's synthesized from multiple sources. If you're not in that synthesis, you might as well not exist. And notice how far down the traditional results have been pushed.

title: Search Evolution Timeline
subtitle: Every Shift Creates New Winners
bullets: 1995: Yahoo Directory → categorization wins • 1998: Google PageRank → links win • 2005: Personalization → relevance wins • 2011: Panda/Penguin → quality wins • 2015: Mobile-first → speed wins • 2018: Voice search → answers win • 2024: AI synthesis → authority wins
speaker_notes: Here's the pattern: every major technological shift in search creates new winners. Directory SEO experts became obsolete. Link spammers got wiped out. Content farms died. The good news? These shifts reward those who adapt quickly. We're in one of those moments right now.

title: We Can't Outrun Algorithms
subtitle: But we can teach them who we are
bullets: We can't outrun the algorithms — but we can teach them who we are.
speaker_notes: Here's the empowering part: you don't have to beat AI - you have to work with it. AI needs sources. It needs authorities. It needs structured, clear, trustworthy information. If you provide that, you become the cited source. Understanding the algorithm gives you control.

title: Very Soon, AI Will Be Everywhere
subtitle: Impact of AI on Search
bullets: The Automation Revolution Is Here
speaker_notes: This isn't coming - it's here. ChatGPT hit 200 million weekly users faster than any product in history. Google's AI Overviews are live. Perplexity is growing exponentially. AI search is becoming the default behavior, especially for younger demographics. Your clients' customers are already using this.

title: 13% → 25.8% AIOs
subtitle: AI Overviews Are Everywhere Now
bullets: Semrush (early 2024): 13% • WebFX Study (2025): 25.8% • Nearly doubled in one year
speaker_notes: In just one year, we've seen AI Overviews nearly double. Semrush reported 13% of searches showed AIOs in early 2024. WebFX's 2025 study shows 25.8%. That's not a trend - that's a takeover. And this number is still growing.

title: CTR Collapse 28% → 19%
subtitle: The #1 Position Isn't What It Used To Be
bullets: 28% CTR for #1 → 19% CTR • 32% decline in clicks to top position
speaker_notes: Here's the devastating impact: The #1 organic position used to get 28% of clicks. Now it's 19%. That's a 32% decline in traffic even when you rank #1. STORY: I consulted with an agency that lost a $15,000/month client who said "Our rankings are up but traffic is down - what are you doing wrong?" The agency wasn't doing anything wrong. The landscape changed. This is the conversation you need to have with every client right now.

title: User Behavior Shift
subtitle: How Users Behave With AI Overviews
bullets: With AIO present: 8% click through • Without AIO: 15% click through • Result: 47% reduction in click behavior
speaker_notes: When an AI Overview appears, user behavior fundamentally changes. Only 8% click through to traditional results, compared to 15% without an AIO. Users trust the AI-generated answer. They don't feel the need to verify. This is why visibility in the AIO itself is critical.

title: Zero-Click Trend 56% → 69%
subtitle: The Rise of Zero-Click Searches
bullets: 56% → 69% of searches end without a click • More than two-thirds have no click • Answer quality matters more than ranking
speaker_notes: This is the macro trend: zero-click searches have grown from 56% to 69%. More than two-thirds of searches now end without anyone clicking on anything. Google answers the question right in the SERP. So the question becomes: Are you the source Google is citing? Are you in that answer?

title: Visibility ≠ Traffic
subtitle: The New Equation
bullets: OLD: Visibility = Rankings → Traffic → Conversions • NEW: Visibility = Citations → Authority → Mindshare → Eventual conversions
speaker_notes: This is the conversation you need to have with every client in Q1 2025. Visibility no longer equals traffic. You can have massive visibility - millions of impressions in AI answers - with zero clicks. But that visibility builds authority, shapes perception, and drives long-term conversions. We have to reframe success metrics.

title: AIO by Query Length
subtitle: Long-Tail Queries Trigger AI Overviews
bullets: 1-2 words: 3.3% show AIO • 3-4 words: 20.1% show AIO • 5-6 words: 35.7% show AIO • 7+ words: 58.2% show AIO
speaker_notes: This is actionable: AI Overviews appear most frequently for long-tail queries. Short queries (1-2 words) only trigger AIOs 3% of the time. But 7+ word queries trigger AIOs 58% of the time. What does this mean for agencies? Long-tail content strategy is now twice as important as it was before. Comprehensive, detailed answers to specific questions win.

title: AIO by Intent
subtitle: Informational Intent Dominates AI Overviews
bullets: Informational: 42% • Commercial: 28% • Transactional: 18% • Navigational: 12%
speaker_notes: AI Overviews appear most frequently for informational queries - the "how do I..." and "what is..." questions. This creates an opportunity: informational content is now your top-of-funnel lead generation engine. Users who get answers from AI still need vendors, partners, solutions. If you're cited in the informational answer, you're top of mind when they're ready to buy.

title: Industry Impact (Health vs Retail)
subtitle: AIO Adoption Varies By Vertical
bullets: Healthcare: 61% • Finance: 48% • Technology: 44% • Retail: 12%
speaker_notes: Not all industries are impacted equally. Healthcare sees AI Overviews on 61% of searches - Google wants to provide immediate health information. Retail? Only 12% - Google wants to drive shopping clicks. Know your vertical's exposure level and adjust strategy accordingly.

title: Client Data Is the New Inventory
subtitle: Agencies: Your Asset Is Client Intelligence
bullets: Client CRM = entity enrichment source • Product catalogs = structured data goldmine • Customer reviews = citation material • Industry knowledge = content authority • First-party data = competitive moat
speaker_notes: For agencies: the data you have access to - your clients' CRMs, product catalogs, customer insights - is your new competitive advantage. This isn't just SEO anymore. You're building knowledge graphs, entity relationships, and authoritative content ecosystems. Treat this data as strategic inventory.

title: AI Isn't Killing SEO — It's Changing Rules
subtitle: New rules create new opportunities
bullets: AI isn't killing SEO — it's changing the rules. And new rules create new opportunities.
speaker_notes: Let's be clear: SEO is not dead. It's evolving. And every evolution creates opportunities for those who adapt. The agencies that are panicking right now? They'll fall behind. The agencies that see this as an opportunity? They'll dominate. Which one will you be?

speaker_notes: Just curious - who here has seen this? Traffic declining even though rankings are stable or improving? (Pause for virtual reactions/chat responses) This is the AI impact in real-time. title: Visual Break
speaker_notes: Alright, we've covered a lot of data. Let's shift gears and talk about how this actually works under the hood.

title: How AI Search Finds and Cites Answers
subtitle: How AI Search Works
bullets: Understanding the AI Search Pipeline
speaker_notes: Let me simplify how AI search works. It's not magic - it's a pipeline. AI retrieves information from trusted sources (Google's index, Wikipedia, high-authority sites), then generates a synthesized answer. The key word: trusted. AI doesn't cite random blogs. It cites sources with strong authority signals. That's your target.

title: LLM vs RAG vs AIO Diagram
subtitle: The Three AI Search Models
bullets: LLM: Pure generation from training data • RAG: Retrieval + generation • AIO: Google's hybrid - index + Gemini
speaker_notes: Three models to understand: 1) LLM - like ChatGPT's base model - generates from what it learned during training. 2) RAG - retrieves current data, then generates - like Perplexity. 3) AIO - Google's approach - pulls from their index AND generates with Gemini. All three need one thing: authoritative source material. That's where you come in.

title: Be the Grounded Source
subtitle: Your Goal: Be the Source AI Trusts
bullets: Clear entity definitions • Structured data (schema) • High-authority backlinks • Accurate, verifiable information • Consistent cross-platform presence
speaker_notes: AI needs "grounded" sources - meaning verifiable, structured, authoritative. If your content is clear, well-marked with schema, backed by authoritative links, and consistent across platforms, AI will trust it and cite it. This is the new SEO playbook.

title: Visibility = Verifiable Entities + Citations
subtitle: The New Visibility Equation
bullets: Verifiable Entities: Clear schema, knowledge graph presence • Citations: Being referenced in AI answers, Wikipedia, authoritative sources • Result: Mindshare, authority, long-term conversions
speaker_notes: Here's your new equation. Visibility equals verifiable entities plus citations. Master entity-based SEO - make sure you're clearly defined in schema and knowledge graphs. Then earn citations - be the source AI references. Do both, and you become the default authority in your space. Agencies who master this can differentiate from commodity SEO shops that are still chasing keywords.

title: SEO Isn't Dead — It Grew a Brain
subtitle: It just evolved
bullets: SEO isn't dead — it just grew a brain.
speaker_notes: EMPHASIZE - say this slower: SEO isn't dead. It just evolved. It went from keyword matching to understanding meaning, context, and relationships. The good news? The fundamentals still matter - maybe more than ever. Which brings me to something critical...

title: ⚠️ Foundation First
subtitle: Before You Optimize for AI... Fix Your Foundation
bullets: Site Speed: Core Web Vitals passing • Mobile-First: Responsive, fast, usable • Clean Schema: Properly implemented structured data • Crawlable Architecture: Clear site structure • Quality Content: Substantive, authoritative baseline
speaker_notes: Quick pause here. I'm seeing a dangerous pattern in the market. Agencies and clients want to jump straight to "AI SEO" but their foundations are broken. Slow sites, poor mobile experience, messy schema, thin content. Here's the truth: AI doesn't fix bad SEO - it amplifies it. If your site is slow, Google's crawler times out and AI has nothing to reference. If your schema is wrong, AI cites you incorrectly. If your content is thin, there's nothing to synthesize. The workflow I'm about to show you ONLY works if your foundations are solid. This isn't sexy, but it's essential. Make sure the basics are right first.

title: The Amplification Effect
subtitle: AI Amplifies Everything - Good and Bad
bullets: GOOD FOUNDATION: Fast site → AI indexes fully, Clear schema → AI understands entities, Quality content → AI cites accurately, Result: Authority multiplied • BAD FOUNDATION: Slow site → AI crawl times out, Broken schema → AI misunderstands, Thin content → AI ignores or hallucinates, Result: Invisibility or worse
speaker_notes: Think of AI as an amplifier. If your foundation is strong, AI amplifies your authority. If your foundation is weak, AI amplifies your weaknesses - or worse, ignores you entirely. Fix the foundation first, then layer on AI optimization.

title: From Keywords to Entities
subtitle: How Google (and AI) Think Now
bullets: Entity recognition and relationships
speaker_notes: For 20 years, we optimized for keywords - strings of text. Now Google and AI understand entities - the actual people, places, things, and concepts. They understand relationships: "Apple the company makes iPhone. Tim Cook is the CEO. Headquarters is in Cupertino." This is how AI builds context and generates answers. Next 7 minutes: the foundation that makes everything else work.

title: What Are Entities?
subtitle: People, Places, Things + Relationships
bullets: Entities are distinct, identifiable concepts • Person: Tim Cook (CEO of Apple) • Place: Cupertino, California (headquarters) • Thing: iPhone (product by Apple) • Concept: Sustainability (corporate value)
speaker_notes: Think of entities as the nouns in Google's understanding of the world. They're not just words - they're things with properties and relationships. When you optimize for entities, you're helping AI understand what you are, what you do, and how you relate to other trusted entities.

title: Entity Graph Example
subtitle: How Entities Connect
bullets: Apple Inc → iPhone (product) → Tim Cook (CEO) → Cupertino (location) → NASDAQ (exchange) → Sustainability (value)
speaker_notes: This is what Google's Knowledge Graph looks like. Apple is connected to iPhone, Tim Cook, Cupertino, etc. When AI generates an answer about Apple, it pulls from this entire relationship network. Your goal: build a similar network around your brand. Define yourself clearly, establish relationships to known entities, and make those relationships explicit through schema and content.

title: Schema Snippet Example
subtitle: Making Entities Machine-Readable
bullets: JSON-LD schema for a local business example
speaker_notes: This is schema markup - structured data that tells Google and AI exactly what you are. It's machine-readable. AI can parse this instantly and understand: Search Influence is a business, located in New Orleans, founded by Will Scott. Without schema, AI has to guess. With schema, AI knows. Implement clean schema on every important page.

title: Best Practice #1: Question First
subtitle: Start with the User's Question
bullets: Examples: ❌ "Our Services" ✅ "How can AI SEO help my business?" • Users search in questions • AI prioritizes question-answer format • Featured snippets favor Q&A structure
speaker_notes: First best practice: structure your content around questions. Users ask "How do I...?" and AI looks for direct answers. Format your content to match. Use H2s as questions, follow with clear answers. This aligns with both user intent and AI's answer-seeking behavior.

title: Best Practice #2: Clear Labels
subtitle: Label Everything Explicitly
bullets: Examples: ❌ "Our approach includes several phases" ✅ "Phase 1: Discovery, Phase 2: Implementation, Phase 3: Optimization" • Clear labels help AI parse and cite accurately
speaker_notes: AI needs clear labels to understand structure. Use bold headers, numbered steps, explicit labels. Think of it like teaching a very smart but literal student - be specific. "Step 1," "Phase 2," "Key Benefit 3." This helps AI extract and cite your content accurately.

title: Best Practice #3: Fast & Smooth
subtitle: Speed and Clarity Win
bullets: Core Web Vitals passing • Mobile-first design • Clean HTML structure • Fast server response time • AI crawlers have limited time budgets
speaker_notes: If your site is slow, AI crawlers time out before fully indexing your content. Core Web Vitals aren't just for user experience - they're for AI crawlability. Fast, clean sites get fully indexed. Slow, messy sites get partial coverage or ignored. Speed matters more than ever.

title: Best Practice #4: Jump to Answer
subtitle: Use Anchor Links and Direct Navigation
bullets: Table of contents with anchor links • Jump-to-section navigation • Clear URL structure • Breadcrumbs • AI can cite specific sections, not just pages
speaker_notes: Make it easy to jump directly to the answer. Use anchor links, tables of contents, clear URL structures. When AI cites you, it can link directly to the relevant section - not just your homepage. This improves citation quality and user experience.

title: Best Practice #5: Source Notes
subtitle: Show Your Work
bullets: Link to original research • Cite authoritative sources • Include publication dates • Show data sources • Builds trust signals
speaker_notes: AI favors content that cites authoritative sources. When you link to .gov, .edu, major publications, and original research, you signal that your content is trustworthy and verifiable. This reduces the risk of AI hallucinating when it references you and increases the likelihood of citation.

title: Trust and Clarity Beat Hallucinations
subtitle: Be the source AI can verify
bullets: Trust and clarity are the antidotes to hallucination. Be the source AI can verify.
speaker_notes: Here's the bottom line for this section: AI hallucinates when it doesn't have clear, trustworthy sources. If your content is structured, cited, fast, and authoritative, AI will use it confidently. You become the grounded source that prevents hallucinations. That's the competitive advantage.

title: The AI SEO Workflow
subtitle: From Creation to Citation
bullets: The Complete Process
speaker_notes: Alright, here's the practical workflow. This is what we use at Search Influence, and you can steal this entire process. It's built on a simple framework: humans do strategy and judgment, AI does research and execution. Let me walk you through each stage.

title: AI Sandwich Framework
subtitle: Human → AI → Human
bullets: Layer 1 (Human): Strategy, goals, brand voice, judgment • Layer 2 (AI): Research, drafting, formatting, optimization • Layer 3 (Human): Editing, refinement, approval, authenticity • Key Principle: AI augments, humans authorize
speaker_notes: This is the AI Sandwich - my favorite framework. Humans set strategy at the top: what are we trying to achieve? What's the brand voice? AI does the heavy lifting in the middle: research, first draft, schema generation, formatting. Then humans refine at the bottom: edit for accuracy, add personality, ensure it sounds like us. AI does the work, you do the thinking. This is how you scale without losing quality or authenticity.

title: Tool Ecosystem
subtitle: The Automation Stack
bullets: Workflow: Make.com, Zapier, n8n • Content & AI: ChatGPT/Claude, Jasper/Copy.ai, Frase/Surfer SEO • Data: Google Sheets, Airtable, Looker Studio • SEO: Schema App, Screaming Frog, Google Search Console
speaker_notes: Here's the tool ecosystem we use. Make and Zapier for workflow automation - connecting APIs and triggering actions. ChatGPT and Claude for content drafting and research. Google Sheets and Airtable for data management. Schema App and Screaming Frog for technical SEO. You don't need all of these - start with one automation workflow and build from there.

title: Automating GBP Posts
subtitle: Real Workflow: GBP Post Automation
bullets: BEFORE: 30 hours/month manually creating posts, Inconsistent formatting, Missed schedules • AFTER: 30 minutes/month managing automation, Consistent brand voice, Never miss a post, 98% time savings • Workflow: Google Sheets → Make.com → ChatGPT → GBP API → Results logged
speaker_notes: STORY TIME - be specific: Let me walk you through a real automation we built. We had a client spending 30 hours a month manually creating Google Business Profile posts. Every week, someone had to write posts, find images, format them, schedule them. We built an automation: content calendar lives in a Google Sheet, Make.com pulls from the sheet, sends to ChatGPT with brand voice guidelines, ChatGPT drafts the post, Make posts it via the GBP API, logs the result. Now it takes 30 minutes a month to manage the sheet. That's 98% time savings. The posts are more consistent, they're never late, and the team focuses on strategy instead of busywork.

title: Entity Enrichment Workflow
subtitle: Building Your Entity Graph
bullets: 1. Extract: Pull entity data from CRM, product catalog, team bios • 2. Match: Map to knowledge graph entities, Wikipedia/Wikidata • 3. Markup: Implement schema.org structured data, JSON-LD • 4. Publish: Deploy sitewide, submit to knowledge bases, monitor
speaker_notes: This is how you build an entity presence systematically. Extract entity data from your client's existing assets - their CRM, product catalogs, team information. Match those entities to known entities in Wikipedia, Wikidata, the knowledge graph. Then markup your site with clean schema so AI can understand the relationships. Finally, publish and monitor. This process turns messy client data into structured, AI-readable entities.

title: Optimization for Snippets & Citations
subtitle: Content Formatting for AI Citation
bullets: STRUCTURE: H2s as questions, Direct answers first, Bulleted lists, Tables for comparisons • TECHNICAL: FAQ schema, HowTo schema, Article schema • CONTENT: Primary question in 40-60 words, Supporting details below, Cited sources, Dates visible
speaker_notes: Format your content to be citation-friendly. AI looks for clear question-answer pairs, structured lists, comparison tables. Use schema to make the structure machine-readable. Answer the primary question in 40-60 words at the top - that's the ideal snippet length. Then provide supporting detail below. This format works for both featured snippets and AI citations.

title: Citation Earning Tactics
subtitle: Building Authority Beyond Your Site
bullets: 1. Earn Media Coverage: PR to tier-1 publications, Expert quotes, Podcast appearances • 2. Directory & Citations: Wikipedia (if notable), Authoritative directories, Review platforms • 3. Thought Leadership: LinkedIn articles, Guest posts, Speaking engagements • 4. Partnerships: Co-marketing, Associations, Awards
speaker_notes: You can't control AI citations on your own site alone - you need external authority signals. Earn media coverage in tier-1 publications - those are heavily weighted in AI training data. Get your brand on Wikipedia if you meet notability guidelines. Build a presence on authoritative industry directories. Publish thought leadership on LinkedIn and high-authority sites. These external citations build the authority that makes AI trust your own content.

title: Agentic AI Efficiency
subtitle: The Next Evolution - AI Agents
bullets: What Are AI Agents? Autonomous AI systems • Examples: Research agent (monitors competitors weekly), Content agent (drafts from keyword opportunities), Reporting agent (generates client reports), Monitoring agent (brand mention alerts) • Impact: No-code implementation, Capacity multiplied, 24/7 operation
speaker_notes: We're moving from AI tools to AI agents - autonomous systems that complete entire workflows. A research agent can monitor your competitors, summarize findings, and email you a report every Monday. A content agent can identify keyword opportunities, draft posts, and save them for your review. These aren't replacing people - they're multiplying capacity. One strategist can manage 3x more clients when AI agents handle the execution.

title: AI Does the Work — You Do the Thinking
subtitle: The future of marketing
bullets: The future of marketing: AI does the work. You do the thinking.
speaker_notes: This is the mindset shift. Stop spending time on tasks AI can do better and faster. Spend your time on what AI can't do: strategy, creativity, client relationships, brand building. Let AI handle research, drafting, formatting, reporting. You handle judgment, refinement, and human connection.

title: Automate Trivial → Amplify Strategic
subtitle: The Agency Leverage Model
bullets: AUTOMATE: Research and data, First drafts, Schema generation, Reporting, Routine updates • HUMANS OWN: Strategic planning, Brand voice, Client relationships, Creative direction, Quality assurance • Result: Higher margins, better work, happier teams
speaker_notes: Here's the agency model going forward. Automate everything that's repeatable and rules-based. Amplify the strategic work that requires judgment and creativity. EXAMPLE: One agency I know automated 80% of their reporting, which freed up 15 hours per week per account manager. Those hours went into proactive strategy sessions with clients. Client retention went up because the relationship got stronger. That's the power of automation - it creates capacity for what actually drives value.

title: Tracking the Invisible
subtitle: Tracking & Measurement
bullets: The New KPIs - Measuring What Matters
speaker_notes: Here's the tracking challenge: when AI answers a question and cites your brand, that doesn't show up in Google Analytics. The user never clicked. But you just influenced their perception, built authority, shaped their decision-making. How do we measure that? We need new infrastructure and new KPIs. Next few minutes: how to track the invisible.

title: GA4 AI Traffic Setup
subtitle: Setting Up AI Referral Tracking
bullets: 1. Create Custom Channel Group: Source contains chatgpt, perplexity, claude, bard, gemini • 2. Custom Dimensions: AI Source, Query Context, User Agent parsing • 3. Create Segment: Filter for AI referral traffic
speaker_notes: First step: set up AI referral tracking in GA4. Create a custom channel group that captures traffic from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and other AI platforms. These show up in your referral data but get buried unless you segment them. Create custom dimensions to capture which AI platform sent the traffic. Then build a segment so you can analyze AI referral behavior separately from organic search. This shows you when AI is actually driving traffic.

title: Looker Dashboard
subtitle: AI Visibility Dashboard
bullets: AI TRAFFIC: Sessions from AI platforms, Conversion rate, Pages per session • VISIBILITY: AIO trigger %, Citation mentions, Featured snippets, Knowledge panel impressions • TRENDS: Week-over-week AI traffic growth, Citation volume, Competitive visibility
speaker_notes: Build a dashboard that shows AI visibility alongside traditional metrics. Track sessions from AI platforms - is that traffic converting? Monitor your AIO trigger rate - what % of your target keywords show AI Overviews, and are you in them? Track citation mentions from tools like Otterly. Watch trends: is AI traffic growing? Are citations increasing? This dashboard tells the real story of your AI presence.

title: Citation Trackers
subtitle: Tools for Monitoring AI Citations
bullets: Otterly.ai: Monitors ChatGPT citations, Brand mentions, Competitor comparison, $99-299/mo • Profound: AI Overview monitoring, Keyword-level visibility, Enterprise pricing • Rankscale: AIO trigger tracking, Featured snippets, SERP features • DIY: Manual testing, Screenshots, Spreadsheet logging
speaker_notes: Several tools are emerging for AI citation tracking. Otterly monitors ChatGPT specifically - it tracks when and how your brand is mentioned in ChatGPT responses. Profound focuses on Google AI Overviews. Rankscale tracks which keywords trigger AIOs and whether you're present. These tools are early-stage and expensive, but they provide visibility you can't get elsewhere. Alternatively, DIY: regularly test key queries in different AI platforms, screenshot when you're cited, log in a spreadsheet. It's manual but it works.

title: KPI Table
subtitle: The Complete AI SEO Scorecard
bullets: AIO Trigger %: Track trend • AIO Presence %: 30%+ is strong • AI Referral Traffic: Month-over-month growth • Citation Mentions: Week-over-week increase • Entity Recognition: Knowledge panel impressions • Featured Snippets: 20%+ of target keywords • Schema Coverage: 100% of key pages • Core Web Vitals: All passing
speaker_notes: Here's your complete scorecard. Track AIO trigger rate - what percentage of your keywords show AI Overviews. Track AIO presence - when AIOs appear, are you in them? Aim for 30%+ presence rate. Monitor AI referral traffic month-over-month. Count citation mentions weekly. Check entity recognition through knowledge panel impressions. Maintain featured snippet ownership. Ensure schema coverage on all important pages. And keep Core Web Vitals passing - speed is the foundation. This scorecard tells you if your AI SEO is working.

title: Traffic = Old Money; Citation = New Money
subtitle: The Currency of Success Has Changed
bullets: OLD CURRENCY: Pageviews, Sessions, Bounce rate, Time on site • NEW CURRENCY: Brand mentions in AI, Entity authority, Citation volume, Mindshare • Both Matter - But Citation Is Leading Indicator
speaker_notes: Think of it this way: traffic is old money, citation is new money. Traffic metrics still matter - conversions happen on your site. But citations are the leading indicator. Being cited in AI answers builds authority and mindshare. That authority drives traffic later when users are ready to engage. Don't abandon traffic metrics, but elevate citation metrics. Citation is the new top-of-funnel.

title: What Gets Measured Grows
subtitle: Even when AI writes the report
bullets: What gets measured grows — even when AI writes the report.
speaker_notes: Establish these tracking systems now. What gets measured improves. If you're not tracking AI visibility, you can't optimize for it. Set up the dashboards, implement the tools, report on the new KPIs. Your clients need to see this data - and so do you.

title: AI SEO Mistakes I'm Seeing
subtitle: Don't Make These Mistakes
bullets: 1. Building on Broken Foundations: Jumping to AI SEO with slow sites, poor UX, messy schema • 2. Tool Obsession Without Strategy: Chasing every AI tool without goals • 3. Abandoning SEO Fundamentals: Thinking AI SEO replaces traditional SEO • 4. Not Leading Client Conversations: Waiting instead of educating • 5. Analysis Paralysis: Waiting for landscape to settle
speaker_notes: I'm seeing agencies make these five mistakes repeatedly. The biggest one - number one - is trying to do AI SEO on top of broken foundations. Clients come to me saying "We want AI optimization" but their site loads in 8 seconds, their mobile experience is terrible, their schema is a mess. AI can't fix that. It amplifies it. If your site is slow, AI crawlers time out. If your schema is wrong, AI cites you incorrectly. Fix the foundation first - speed, structure, schema, quality content - THEN layer on AI optimization. Second: tool obsession without strategy. Third: some think AI SEO replaces traditional SEO - it doesn't, it builds on it. Fourth: waiting for clients to ask instead of leading. title: Agentic AI Is Here
